summary: Old Mission Point's 1870 keeper's dwelling and tower, staffed until 1933 and replaced in 1938 by an offshore light; now township property with keeper stays.

access.note: Grounds are township property. Visits run through an overnight keeper program and a seasonal shop; an older Terry Pepper page says the grounds were closed to the public.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Staffing ended on 30 June 1933 and an automated acetylene light took over (LighthouseFriends); the old lighthouse was deactivated in 1938, when the offshore Mission Point Light replaced it (LighthouseFriends). The record's 1933 and 1938 dates both stand, for keepers and for the light's function.

Terry Pepper says the State of Michigan bought the old property after the Second World War; LighthouseFriends says most of the reservation went to Michigan for a park in 1931 and the township bought the lighthouse in 1948. The LighthouseFriends account is used.

notes_for_editor: NRHP: the cached nomination for NRHP 80004798 is a PNG placeholder (about 1,000 characters), so no nomination facts are used; a human may want the nomination once digitised. NAMES: USLHS prints Jerome M. Pratt, Jr.; Terry Pepper and LighthouseFriends print Jerome M. Pratt (Sr.). USLHS and LighthouseFriends print John M. McHarry; Terry Pepper prints John M. McHaney. LighthouseFriends prints Sara E. Lane; USLHS prints Sarah E. Lane. DISPUTE: McHarry's death: LighthouseFriends says he drowned on 1 August 1881 after going over the side of the steamer City of Traverse; Terry Pepper gives 15 August 1881 with no cause (the story says both). OWNERSHIP: see resolved_conflicts. ACCESS: Terry Pepper (older) says the dwelling and grounds are closed; LighthouseFriends says the interior opened in 2008; the USLHS lists a keeper stay; the station record says public. Current status not verified on site. RECORD EVENTS NOT USED: the record's 1895 first light (Rowlett) and 1907 'Tower 2' are not in Terry Pepper or LighthouseFriends; the 1907 tower is not used. SAME NAME: Lighthouse Board reports refer to North Passage (Mission Point), Mackinac Island; a different place, not used. STORMS: no storm, wreck or rescue tied to the light was found in the sources read; no newspaper search was run for this station, so the Storms chapter is omitted. A 1889 Life-Saving Service report names a schooner sailing from Old Mission Point; it is not a station event and is not used. The USLHS accommodations listing names the operator's manager; the story does not name them. Keeper roster: roster.py matched mission-point-old by name and position (0.10 km); 7 lines. Dates in accessed fields use the system clock (2026-10-27); the task brief says 2026-10-22. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-22: Terry Pepper and LighthouseFriends prose is paraphrased (short quotations only). Davenport's 'sixty year old' and March 13, 1907 date are cited to Pepper, and his McGulpin's Point service (1879-1906) is stated. Ownership disagreement is now stated in Today: Pepper says the State of Michigan bought the property after the Second World War; LighthouseFriends says the township owns it, with the 1931 park transfer and the 1948 purchase by residents. The McHaney (Pepper) / McHarry (LighthouseFriends and roster) spelling is stated. Focal plane is 47 ft (Pepper) against 48 ft (LighthouseFriends); the story does not use it.
